abaddon.title: Abaddon
abaddon.about: A male deity/angel in the New Testament
abaddon.note: The name means destruction. In Revelation it belongs to the angel ruling the locusts out of the abyss, and everywhere else in the Old Testament the same word is just ruin, not a being with a name.

almighty.title: Almighty
almighty.note: It translates El Shaddai, a Hebrew title for God used most in the stories of the patriarchs and in Job. It describes who God is and what he can do, and it is not anyone's name.

antipas.title: Antipas
antipas.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
antipas.note: Revelation 2:13 calls him a faithful martyr, killed at Pergamum, the city "where Satan's seat is." He is not Herod Antipas the tetrarch.

apollyon.title: Apollyon
apollyon.about: A male deity/angel in the New Testament
apollyon.note: The name means Destroyer. John gives it in Revelation 9:11 to the angel over the locust creatures from the abyss, the Greek for Abaddon in the same verse.

aser.title: Aser
aser.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
aser.note: The Greek form of Asher, Jacob's eighth son. Luke uses it for the tribe of the prophetess Anna, and Revelation 7:6 lists it among the sealed tribes.

asia.title: Asia
asia.note: Not the continent. The Roman province of Asia, in western Asia Minor, with Ephesus among its churches, and the region the seven churches of Revelation belonged to.

balaam.title: Balaam
balaam.about: Prophet living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
balaam.note: A prophet, but not an Israelite. Balak of Moab hired him to curse the Israelites. On the way his donkey saw an angel blocking the road that Balaam himself missed, and God made the animal speak to rebuke him.

balac.title: Balac
balac.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
balac.note: Balak in Greek, brought up in Revelation 2:14 when Christ rebukes the church at Pergamum for tolerating teaching that echoes Balaam's.

benjamin.title: Benjamin
benjamin.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
benjamin.note: Jacob's twelfth son and the youngest, born to Rachel on the road near Bethlehem as she died giving birth to him. Jacob guarded him fiercely after losing Joseph. That fear drives much of the tension in Joseph's story.

christ.title: Christ
christ.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
christ.note: A title, not a surname. It is the Greek for the Hebrew Messiah, the anointed one, and the New Testament gives it to Jesus of Nazareth as the king, priest and deliverer the Old Testament promised. His life and ministry are under Jesus.

david.title: David
david.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
david.note: The shepherd from Bethlehem who killed Goliath and became Israel's second king, ruling a kingdom bigger than any native king held before or after. Solomon was one of his sons. Nearly half the psalms carry his name, and the Tel Dan inscription, where an enemy king boasts over the house of David, put his dynasty outside the Bible as well.

ephesus.title: Ephesus
ephesus.note: The chief city of Roman Asia, with the temple of Artemis and a theatre for some twenty five thousand. Paul stayed about three years and the silversmiths rioted over lost trade. Later it was one of the seven churches of Revelation, and tradition says John died and was buried there.

euphrates.title: Euphrates
euphrates.note: The great river. It rises in the Armenian highlands and runs some seventeen hundred miles to the Persian Gulf. Genesis has it as one of Eden's four rivers, the promise to Abraham reaches to it, and later Assyria and Babylon came from beyond it.

gad.title: Gad
gad.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
gad.note: Jacob's seventh son, born to Leah's servant Zilpah. His tribe asked for good pasture east of the Jordan and got it. The condition was that Gad's fighting men still crossed over and helped the other tribes take their land first.

greek.title: Greek
greek.note: Here it means the language, not the people. It is one of the three on the sign Pilate had nailed above Jesus.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

issachar.title: Issachar
issachar.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
issachar.note: Jacob's ninth son. His tribe held the fertile Jezreel Valley, and Chronicles says its men understood the times and knew what Israel ought to do.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jesus.title: Jesus
jesus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
jesus.note: Born in Bethlehem to Mary and raised in Nazareth in Galilee. Around thirty he began teaching in parables, healing, and gathering twelve disciples, until he was arrested in Jerusalem at Passover, tried before the council and Pontius Pilate, and crucified. His followers said he rose bodily three days later, and the New Testament names him the Messiah, God's own Son become human.

jezabel.title: Jezabel
jezabel.about: Queen living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jezabel.note: This is a woman in the church at Thyatira, not the old queen. She called herself a prophetess and taught believers to commit sexual immorality and eat food sacrificed to idols, and John hangs the queen's name on her to say what kind of influence she was.

john-2.title: John
john-2.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
john-2.note: Zebedee's son and James's younger brother, a fisherman, and with Peter and James one of the three who saw what the rest did not, the transfiguration and Gethsemane among it. From the cross Jesus gave him his mother Mary to look after. Tradition makes him the disciple Jesus loved and credits him with the fourth Gospel, three letters, and Revelation, written in exile on Patmos.

joseph.title: Joseph
joseph.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
joseph.note: Jacob's eleventh son and Rachel's first. His father's favouritism and his own tactless dreams got him sold into Egypt by his brothers, and there he rose from slave to prisoner to second in the land by reading Pharaoh's dreams of famine. When the famine drove his brothers down for grain, he told them who he was and forgave them.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

laodicea.title: Laodicea
laodicea.note: A rich banking and cloth city in the Lycus Valley. It had no water of its own and piped it in from the hot springs at Hierapolis and the cold springs at Colossae, so it arrived lukewarm, and Revelation's "neither cold nor hot" plays on that. Its church gets the sharpest rebuke of the seven.

levi.title: Levi
levi.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
levi.note: Jacob's third son. He and Simeon massacred the men of Shechem after their sister Dinah was raped, and Jacob cursed them both for it on his deathbed. Even so, Levi's descendants became Israel's priestly tribe, given service at the tabernacle instead of land, partly for their zeal against the golden calf at Sinai.

manasses-2.title: Manasses
manasses-2.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
manasses-2.note: The Greek form of Manasseh. Here it is the tribe, counted among the sealed in Revelation.

nephthalim.title: Nephthalim
nephthalim.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
nephthalim.note: The Greek spelling of Naphtali. Matthew uses it for the land where a people in darkness see a great light, as Jesus begins his work there.

nicolaitane.title: Nicolaitane
nicolaitane.about: Religious group in the New Testament
nicolaitane.note: Christ condemns them twice in the letters of Revelation, once to Ephesus and once to Pergamum. Their teaching or practice was tied to idolatry and sexual immorality, and that is about all the text gives us.

omega.title: Omega
omega.note: Last letter of the Greek alphabet, paired with Alpha. Revelation puts the pair in God's own mouth, three times over.

patmos.title: Patmos
patmos.note: John was on Patmos, a small rocky island in the Aegean off Asia Minor, when he saw the visions in Revelation.

pergamos.title: Pergamos
pergamos.note: One of the seven churches of Revelation sat here, and Christ commends it for holding fast to his name in the place Revelation calls "Satan's seat." That is likely the city's huge altar to Zeus.

philadelphia.title: Philadelphia
philadelphia.note: The church in Philadelphia had little strength and kept the faith anyway, and Revelation praises it for that. The city stood in Lydia in Asia Minor, close to a fault line, and earthquakes hit it again and again.

reuben.title: Reuben
reuben.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
reuben.note: Jacob's firstborn. He slept with one of his father's concubines and lost the birthright for it, and Jacob had not forgotten it on his deathbed.

sardis.title: Sardis
sardis.note: The church at Sardis got one of the seven letters in Revelation. The city had been the rich capital of Lydia in western Asia Minor, the seat of King Croesus, and known for refining gold.

satan.title: Satan
satan.about: An angel in the Old Testament
satan.note: The name means adversary. In Job he questions whether Job's goodness is real, and in Zechariah he stands to accuse Joshua the high priest before the angel of the Lord.

simeon.title: Simeon
simeon.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
simeon.note: Jacob's second son. With his brother Levi he killed the men of Shechem after their sister Dinah was raped. Jacob held it against them on his deathbed.

smyrna.title: Smyrna
smyrna.note: About forty miles north of Ephesus, on the coast of Asia Minor. The church at Smyrna was one of the seven in Revelation, and it got no rebuke, only a warning that suffering was coming.

thyatira.title: Thyatira
thyatira.note: A trading city in the Roman province of Asia, known for its guilds, especially the dyers. Lydia, the seller of purple cloth Paul met at Philippi, came from there, and Revelation sends one of its seven letters to the church there.

zabulon.title: Zabulon
zabulon.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
zabulon.note: The Greek form of Zebulun. Matthew uses it for the country where Jesus started preaching after he left Nazareth for Capernaum, and Revelation counts it among the sealed tribes.
